characters.summary: Kingdom Come Batman is an aged Bruce Wayne whose body is so damaged by years of crime-fighting that he depends on a surgically attached exoskeleton. He guards Gotham with Batman-themed robots and drones from the Batcave and leads his own network of heroes (the Silent Cavalry), preferring strategy and command to direct brawling.

techniques: Command of Batman-themed robots and robotic drones
Martial arts and detective skill (limited by his injuries)
Leading the Silent Cavalry and his metahuman agents

mechanisms: Battle suit built by his employees

weaknesses: Aged physical condition and reliance on spinal exoskeleton support
limitations: Injuries limit his own fighting; he stays mostly confined to the Batcave in old age
characters.formDifferences: Represents an older, physically degraded Bruce Wayne who uses a mechanical spine brace and automated security forces.

sources.supports: Batman forms the Silent Cavalry, reluctantly allies with Luthor's Mankind Liberation Front, then ambushes it; Superman confronts him to persuade him, not to fight; Batman later turns Wayne Manor into a hospital; his mechanized exosuit.

Surgically attached exoskeleton and later back brace due to years of injuries; Batman-themed robots protecting Gotham and robotic drones; battle suit; martial arts, detective and computer skills; mostly confined to the Batcave.

unknowns: No documented one-on-one fight result in Kingdom Come; the earlier claim of a Kingdom Come #3 loss to Superman was removed because Superman only confronts him verbally (Batman does not fight Superman or Wonder Woman).
Full extent of automated defenses deployed in the Batcave.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Dark Multiverse (Dark Nights: Metal and The Batman Who Laughs)
characters.summary: The Batman Who Laughs is a Dark Multiverse Bruce Wayne transformed by Joker toxin. He combines Batman's planning with Joker's sadism, using machine guns, knives, a bladed chain, Dark Metal batarangs and a precognitive Dark Metal visor, and turns toxin-infected children into his Rabid Robins.

techniques: Machine guns, knives and a bladed chain
Dark Metal batarangs that bring out a victim's worst self

mechanisms: Dark Metal visor granting a form of precognition

weaknesses: Vulnerable to Nth Metal, like other Dark Multiverse inhabitants
limitations: Relies heavily on elaborate planning and subordinate minions
characters.formDifferences: Combines Bruce Wayne's intellect with Joker toxin madness and multiversal Dark Multiverse resources.

sources.supports: Debut in the Dark Nights: Metal crossover; machine guns, knives, bladed chain; Dark Metal batarangs and precognitive Dark Metal visor; Joker toxin and the Rabid Robins; vulnerability to Nth Metal; defeated by a Batman given a Joker transfusion and locked in the Hall of Justice.

unknowns: Removed an unsupported claim that he defeated the Justice League in Dark Nights: Metal #1; the source does not describe that and Metal #1 predates his main role.
His defeat by Batman (after Batman took a Joker transfusion) is described in the source without an issue number; add as a notable result once the issue is pinned.
Exact immunity limits against telepathic intrusion.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Dark Nights: Death Metal
characters.summary: The Darkest Knight is the Batman Who Laughs after he incapacitated Doctor Manhattan and took over the body of Batmanhattan, a Bruce Wayne who had replicated Manhattan's powers. With god-like power and ever more absorbed Crisis energy, he trapped and killed Perpetua and tried to remake the Multiverse before Wonder Woman destroyed him.

techniques: Realigning worlds and deploying his evil Earths

mechanisms: God-like durability derived from Doctor Manhattan's powers

weaknesses: Can be overpowered by Superboy-Prime's blows and by Wonder Woman in a sustained fight
limitations: Power partly depends on absorbed Crisis energy and on the Mobius Chair rigged to feed him
characters.formDifferences: The Batman Who Laughs in Batmanhattan's body, with Doctor Manhattan-derived god-like powers instead of the base form's gear and toxin.

sources.supports: Transformation via Doctor Manhattan / Batmanhattan's body; god-like powers, Crisis energy absorption and the rigged Mobius Chair; traps Perpetua in Source Wall fragments and kills her (Death Metal #6); felled by Superboy-Prime's punches; Wonder Woman punches him into the sun and kills him in the Death Sun.

notableResults.note: Trapped Perpetua in fragments of the Source Wall and killed her, realigning Prime Earth.

notableResults.citation: Dark Nights: Death Metal (finale; issue not stated in source)
notableResults.note: After a fight across time and space, Wonder Woman punched him into Earth's sun and then shoved him into the Death Sun, killing him.

unknowns: Corrected: he was not made from Perpetua's brain; his brain went into Batmanhattan's body.
Flight and teleportation are assumed from Doctor Manhattan-derived powers, not documented in the cited source.
Full extent of dominion over higher-dimensional realms.

characters.summary: Batwoman (Kate Kane) is a West Point-trained former cadet with special-operations training, many martial arts and expert marksmanship. She fights in dilatant armor with a gliding, bladed cape, S-shaped throwing blades and gauntlet tasers, relying on skill and gear rather than powers.

techniques: Martial arts (Krav Maga, Muay Thai, Wing Chun and others)

mechanisms: Cowl with thermal imaging and anti-hypnosis

weaknesses: Human physiology susceptible to conventional injury and trauma
limitations: Relies on standard human endurance and manufactured gear

sources.supports: Military background, equipment, and combat style of Batwoman (Kate Kane).
Military and special-operations training, martial arts, marksmanship; armor, gliding bladed cape, throwing blades, gauntlet tasers, Red Knight One motorcycle; fights vs Alice, Clayface and others.

notableResults.note: After nonlethal attempts failed, killed him with a rifle that destabilized his matter.
Defeated Alice's subordinates and stopped her chemical attack; Alice fell from the plane after stabbing Kate's wrist.

campaignTags.claim: Her father built her a suit and an arsenal of experimental weapons based on Batman's gadgetry, including throwing blades and gauntlet tasers.
Her composite nanotube cape is used for gliding.

unknowns: Replaced a vague 'Hydrology' result: the sources name the collection but not its opponents or outcomes.
Effectiveness against metahumans with high-tier durability.

characters.continuity: DC Comics - Modern Post-Crisis / DC Rebirth
characters.summary: Beast Boy (Garfield Logan) can turn into any animal he has seen, including extinct ones such as a T. rex, in about a second, from insects and mice to elephants. He gains each animal's abilities, such as flight as a bird and water breathing as a fish, and has a healing factor.

techniques: Large predator and prehistoric forms (T. rex, elephant)

mechanisms: Healing factor (recovers from bullet wounds, burns and broken bones in seconds)
Evasion through flying or small forms

weaknesses: Retains human psychological vulnerabilities and animal instincts if overwhelmed
limitations: Cannot take a form that does not fit the space around him
Larger forms used to physically exhaust him

sources.supports: Animal transformations incl. extinct ones, size range (insects to T. rex), flight as birds, water breathing as fish, healing factor, and limits on space and fatigue.

conditional.dependsOn: Transforming into a flying or aquatic animal

campaignTags.claim: Transforms into forms far larger than himself (elephant, T. rex) and very small ones (mice, insects, arachnids).
Gains flight when he becomes a bird.
Gains aquatic breathing when he becomes a fish.
Gains aquatic breathing when he becomes a fish.
Healing factor lets him recover from bullet wounds, burns and broken bones in seconds.
